name: Grusch Congressional testimony
summary: El ex oficial de inteligencia David Grusch testificó bajo juramento ante el Congreso que múltiples fuentes primarias le describieron programas no divulgados de recuperación de material no humano; el Inspector General de la IC calificó su denuncia de 'creíble y urgente'. Testimonio de oídas, pero multifuente.
summary_en: Former intelligence officer David Grusch testified under oath before Congress that multiple firsthand sources described undisclosed programs recovering non-human material; the IC Inspector General deemed his complaint 'credible and urgent'. Hearsay testimony, but multi-source.
whatHappened:
El 26 de julio de 2023, David Charles Grusch, ex-oficial de inteligencia de la USAF (Air Force) con asignación previa al National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency y al UAPTF (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force) desde 2019 a 2021, testificó bajo juramento ante el subcomité de National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs del House Oversight Committee.

Grusch declaró bajo juramento que durante su servicio recibió información de múltiples testigos primarios indicando la existencia de un 'programa de recuperación e ingeniería inversa' de vehículos de origen no humano operado por contratistas del Departamento de Defensa por décadas, no autorizado al Congreso, y que él había referido evidencia específica al Inspector General de la Intelligence Community (ICIG). El ICIG, Thomas Monheim, había evaluado las complaints como 'credible and urgent' en julio 2022 — designación que activa procesos legales específicos.

Grusch también declaró que algunos testigos reportaron 'restos biológicos no humanos' recuperados junto con los artefactos. Especificó que su testimonio era de oídas y multifuente (no observación personal directa) pero que los testigos primarios estaban dispuestos a testificar en sesión SCIF (clasificada). Junto a Grusch testificaron los pilotos navales David Fravor (Nimitz 2004) y Ryan Graves (Atlantic 2014-2015).
whatHappened_en:
On July 26, 2023, David Charles Grusch — a former USAF intelligence officer previously assigned to the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and to the UAPTF (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force) from 2019 to 2021 — testified under oath before the House Oversight Committee's Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs.

Grusch stated under oath that during his service he received information from multiple primary witnesses indicating the existence of a 'recovery and reverse-engineering program' of vehicles of non-human origin, operated by Department of Defense contractors for decades, unauthorized to Congress, and that he had referred specific evidence to the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG). ICIG Thomas Monheim had assessed the complaints as 'credible and urgent' in July 2022 — a designation that triggers specific legal processes.

Grusch further stated that some witnesses reported 'non-human biologics' recovered alongside the artifacts. He specified that his testimony was multi-source hearsay (not direct personal observation) but that the primary witnesses were willing to testify in a SCIF (classified) session. Naval aviators David Fravor (Nimitz 2004) and Ryan Graves (Atlantic 2014-2015) testified alongside Grusch.
whyMatters: Primer testimonio bajo juramento ante el Congreso por un ex-oficial de inteligencia identificado nominalmente, afirmando la existencia de programas no divulgados de recuperación de NHI (Non-Human Intelligence). La calificación 'credible and urgent' del ICIG es un acto administrativo formal que precondiciona la legislación posterior (Schumer/Rounds UAP Disclosure Act 2023-2024) y establece un piso legal para investigaciones congresionales activas que continúan a 2026. El coronel retirado Karl Nell, ex asesor del Grupo de Trabajo UAP, corroboró públicamente el testimonio de Grusch en 2023 sin contradicción institucional — el primer militar de ese rango en hacerlo.
whyMatters_en: The first sworn congressional testimony by a named former intelligence officer asserting the existence of undisclosed NHI (Non-Human Intelligence) recovery programs. The ICIG's 'credible and urgent' rating is a formal administrative act that conditions subsequent legislation (Schumer/Rounds UAP Disclosure Act 2023-2024) and establishes a legal floor for active congressional investigations continuing into 2026. Retired Colonel Karl Nell, a former adviser to the UAP Task Force, publicly corroborated Grusch's testimony in 2023 with no institutional contradiction — the first officer of that rank to do so.

evidenceContribution.rationale: Testimonio bajo juramento ante el Congreso de EE.UU. + estatus protegido como denunciante por la Inspector General de la Comunidad de Inteligencia (ICIG) + corroboración cruzada con notas Wilson-Davis. La narrativa Grusch describe explícitamente programas no-divulgados.
evidenceContribution.rationaleEn: Sworn testimony before the U.S. Congress + protected whistleblower status from the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG) + cross-corroboration with Wilson-Davis notes. The Grusch narrative explicitly describes non-disclosed programs.

evidenceContribution.rationale: Grusch declaró bajo juramento la existencia de material recuperado de origen no humano y restos biológicos. El testimonio jurado eleva el peso epistémico aunque la evidencia material primaria no ha sido producida públicamente.
evidenceContribution.rationaleEn: Grusch testified under oath to the existence of recovered material of non-human origin and biological remains. Sworn testimony raises the epistemic weight even though primary material evidence has not been publicly produced.

evidenceContribution.rationale: La narrativa de programas de recuperación con cadena de custodia federal es incompatible con explicación natural — si el testimonio es falso, lo es por mala fe o error, no por confusión con un fenómeno natural.
evidenceContribution.rationaleEn: The narrative of retrieval programs with federal chain of custody is incompatible with a natural explanation — if the testimony is false, it is so by bad faith or error, not by confusion with a natural phenomenon.
